issues.title: Diagonal convolution does not regularize all spatial variables

failure_location.quote: v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e)

issues.failure_explanation: The construction is required to produce a smooth function of all 3d spatial variables, but it convolves only along (e,e,e). For d=1, the admissible bounded Lipschitz function v(t,x,y,z)=min(1,|x-y|) is unchanged by the spatial averaging and remains nonsmooth at x=y. Thus the claimed smooth derivatives used later are not available.
issues.overall_effect: The regularized inputs used in the consistency and comparison argument need not possess the independent x-, y-, and z-derivatives required by the proof, leaving the main error theorem and its rate consequences unestablished.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the diagonal spatial averaging by a standard mollifier on R^{3d}: write e=(e_x,e_y,e_z), use v(t−τ,x−e_x,y−e_y,z−e_z), and normalize it with ε^{−(2+3d)}. Re-establish the standard finite-order derivative estimates and use the independent spatial-translation invariance of both the PIDE and the recursive scheme to carry the comparison proof and all four dependent results through, changing only constants.
issues.why_classification: The claimed smoothing is genuinely false, so this is not a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, full-dimensional convolution is a short, standard, source-supported replacement; it requires no new lemma, hypothesis, proof architecture, or rate optimization, and preserves every affected guarantee up to immaterial constants.

issues.title: One-sided mollification evaluates v beyond terminal time

failure_location.quote: \int_{-\varepsilon^{2}}^{0} \int_{|e| < \varepsilon} v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e)

issues.failure_explanation: For t>1-epsilon^2, part of the integration region has t-tau>1; at t=1 every negative tau does. Those values lie outside the declared domain of v, so the mollification and its estimates are not defined on the full interval required by the comparison proof.
issues.overall_effect: The regularized u and u_h are undefined near the terminal time under the old construction, so the comparison argument on [h,1] and all stated terminal-time rate consequences lack valid inputs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Give a Hölder function v a constant extension beyond t=1 so that the displayed convolution and its regularity estimates are defined. In the PIDE and scheme arguments, use the mollified comparison only on t≤1−ε², where every translated time remains in the original domain, and transfer the estimate to the terminal strip [1−ε²,1] using the established temporal regularity of u and u_h. The resulting O(ε+h^{1/2}) contribution can be absorbed into the existing error terms in the main theorem and all rate consequences.
issues.why_classification: The missing terminal-time treatment is a genuine domain defect, not a typo. It is resolved by a routine extension and boundary-strip argument, with no change to the model class, conclusions, or convergence exponents and only a change of constants.

issues.title: Mollifier constant ranges over infinitely many derivative orders
issues.failure_explanation: The old assertion defines K_zeta as a finite maximum over all i+j>=1. A nonzero compactly supported smooth mollifier cannot have uniformly bounded L1 norms for derivatives of every order, so the asserted finite common constant and the all-order estimate are false as written.
issues.overall_effect: The preliminary all-order estimate is false, and the K_zeta-dependent error constants in the main proof are not finite as defined. The proof itself requires only finitely many derivative orders.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For the all-order mollification estimate, use the order-dependent constant K_{i,j}=||∂_t^i D^jζ||_1. For the downstream proof, define K_ζ as the maximum of these constants over the finite set of derivative pairs actually used, all satisfying i+j≤3, and use that finite K_ζ in the stated error constants.
issues.why_classification: The old proof explicitly uses no derivative beyond total order three, so the omitted finite cutoff in the common constant is forced directly by the source. Higher-order estimates remain valid with their order-dependent constants, and no inference, construction, theorem, or rate needs repair; this is finite-constant transcription rather than mathematical work.

issues.title: Pointwise consistency does not supply a global comparison error
issues.failure_explanation: The prose and formulas of the proof require a scalar E_1(epsilon,h) or E_2(epsilon,h) that bounds the consistency error at every comparison point. The old assumption claims only that, for each fixed (p,A,phi), l_phi(s) tends to zero uniformly in z. In the proof, p=D_y omega, A=D_x^2 omega, and phi=omega(t,x,y,z+·) range over a family, and u_h^epsilon itself varies with h. Pointwise convergence supplies neither a finite common supremum nor convergence of that supremum, so the global comparison estimate does not follow.
issues.overall_effect: The general main error theorem and its universal-limit corollary are unsupported under the old assumptions. The later H1-H2 example derives an explicit derivative-norm-controlled modulus, so its specialized rate results do not depend on the missing generic uniformity and are not listed as affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the consistency premise to provide a modulus l̂(s,L) that tends to zero uniformly in z and uniformly over all (p,A,φ) satisfying |p|+|A|+||φ||_∞+Σ_{k=1}^3||D^kφ||_∞≤L, for every fixed L. Use the mollification bounds to select a global L in the consistency lemma, thereby making E_1 and E_2 scalar bounds valid at every comparison point, and propagate those bounds to the main theorem and its universal-limit corollary. The explicit H1–H2 examples already supply such a derivative-controlled modulus.
issues.why_classification: Pointwise consistency does not entail the required uniform bound, and imposing uniformity over a bounded C^3 family is a genuine strengthening that excludes coherent pointwise-only input models, so the repair exceeds a minor technical edit. The strengthening is nevertheless contained: it leaves the comparison architecture and the same conclusions and rates intact for a recognizably comparable class, including the paper's explicit examples, and therefore does not require global reconstruction or major mathematical loss.

issues.title: Mollification estimate omits the grid-jump term
issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims ||u_h-u_h^epsilon||_infinity<=2C_0 epsilon from Lemma uh_regularity(ii), although that lemma controls time increments by C_0(|t-s|^{1/2}+h^{1/2}). Since u_h is piecewise constant, it can jump by order h^{1/2} at a grid point. For example, with centered X taking values +/-1 and bounded Lipschitz phi(x)=min(1,|x|), the first-step value at x=0 differs from the preceding interval by h^{1/2}. A convolution crossing that interface therefore need not approach u_h uniformly at order epsilon alone.
issues.overall_effect: The lower comparison bound in the main theorem has an invalid mollification step and understated constants. Its universal-limit corollary and the later two-sided rate results rely on that bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the mollification bounds by ||u_h−u_h^ε||_∞≤C C_0(ε+h^{1/2}) and ||∂_t^lD^ku_h^ε||_∞≤C C_0K_ζ(ε+h^{1/2})ε^{−2l−k}. Insert these bounds into E_1 and the lower comparison argument and update the constants in the main theorem and its dependents. In the specialized optimization ε=h^Γ, the established Γ<1/2 gives h^{1/2}≤ε for small h, so the additional term is absorbed and all stated convergence exponents remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The omitted grid-jump term makes the displayed inference genuinely invalid, so it is not a typo. The correction follows immediately from the paper's own time-regularity lemma and requires only local estimate and constant bookkeeping; it introduces no new hypothesis, lemma, architecture, or loss of rate.
